Strategy: Represent reductions as finite paths and prove a **strip lemma**: a single step from \(x\) can be joined with any finite path from \(x\). Induct along that path, using the local hypothesis to tile each encountered fork; the “at most one step” residual is what can be passed to the next tile without increasing complexity.

Then induct on the length of one of the two original paths. Peel off its first step, apply the strip lemma against the other path, and apply the induction hypothesis to the remaining tail. Zero-length paths give the base cases. The one-step bound is essential: ordinary local joinability by two arbitrary finite paths does not imply confluence without an additional assumption such as termination.
